To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We report the identification and characterization of a rice homolog of HKT1, the wheat high affinity K+-uptake transporter, which shows transport characteristics similar to those of HKT1 but also mediates transport of Na+ and other alkali cation.

we have cloned a rice HKT-type transporter that is able to transport K+, Rb+, Na+, Li+, and to some extent, Cs+ and that the expression of this gene is downregulated in response to salt and other alkali cation stress in rice.

the expression of the rice homolog of the wheat K+/ Na+ transporter HKT1 in roots is repressed by Na+ and other alkali cation ions, and that differences in the expression of the transporter in salt-sensitive and salt-tolerant plants are observed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a rice HKT-type transporter as a general alkalin cation transporter.
a transporter which mediates K+ and Na+ uptake in plants and is involved in the regulation of Na+ and K+ homeostasis in rice.
the characterization of rice HKT transporters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OsHKT1 may play a role in Na+ and K+ uptake in rice, but the precise physiological function is still unclear and needs further investigation.
HKT1 is an important gene for salt tolerance.
HKT-type transporters are general cation transporters with a strong affinity for Na+, and are involved in Na+ homeostasis and Na+ exclusion in plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the rice gene OsHKT1, when expressed in a heterologous system, can transport K+ and Na+.

OsHKT1 functions as a general alkalin cation transporter and that the control over its expression in space and in time may be a factor that may differentiate salt stress-sensitive and -tolerant plants.
we have identified a HKT-type Na+ and K+ transporter in rice that is expressed in the vascular system in leaves and roots.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rice HKT transporter is a general cation transporter and not specific for K+ as previously suggested.
the HKT-type transporters are not restricted to K+ and Na+ transport, but also function in the transport of other cations, such as Rb+, Li+ and Cs+.
OsHKT1, like HKT1 in other species, can mediate uptake of K+ and other alkali cation species.
